sanskrit: tau kabandhena taṃ mārgaṃ pampāyā darśitaṃ vane ātasthatur diśaṃ gṛhya pratīcīṃ nṛvarātmajau
english: Those two sons of the best of kings, having received from Kabandha the path to Pampā shown in the forest, set out taking the western direction.

sanskrit: tau śaileṣv ācitānekān kṣaudrakalpaphaladrumān vīkṣantau jagmatur draṣṭuṃ sugrīvaṃ rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, beholding the many trees on the hills laden with honey-like fruits, proceeded in order to meet Sugrīva.

sanskrit: kṛtvā ca śailapṛṣṭhe tu tau vāsaṃ raghunandanau pampāyāḥ paścimaṃ tīraṃ rāghavāv upatasthatuḥ
english: Having spent the night on the ridge of a mountain, the two descendants of Raghu approached the western bank of Pampā.

sanskrit: tau puṣkariṇyāḥ pampāyās tīram āsādya paścimam apaśyatāṃ tatas tatra śabaryā ramyam āśramam
english: Reaching the western bank of the lotus-filled Pampā, those two then saw there the lovely hermitage of Śabarī.

sanskrit: tau tam āśramam āsādya drumair bahubhir āvṛtam suramyam abhivīkṣantau śabarīm abhyupeyatuḥ
english: Approaching that hermitage, surrounded by many trees, and gazing upon its great beauty, the two went up to Śabarī.

sanskrit: tau tu dṛṣṭvā tadā siddhā samutthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ pādau jagrāha rāmasya lakṣmaṇasya ca dhīmataḥ
english: Upon seeing those two, that accomplished female ascetic rose up with palms joined in reverence and clasped the feet of Rāma and of the wise Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: tām uvāca tato rāmaḥ śramaṇīṃ saṃśitavratām kaccit te nirjitā vighnāḥ kaccit te vardhate tapaḥ
english: Rāma then spoke to that female ascetic, firm in her vows: "Have your obstacles been overcome? Does your austerity grow?

sanskrit: kaccit te niyataḥ kopa āhāraś ca tapodhane kaccit te niyamāḥ prāptāḥ kaccit te manasaḥ sukham kaccit te guruśuśrūṣā saphalā cārubhāṣiṇi
english: Have your anger and diet been subdued, O treasure of austerity? Have your religious observances been fulfilled? Is your mind at peace? Has your devoted service to your teacher borne fruit, O fair-spoken one?"

sanskrit: rāmeṇa tāpasī pṛṣṭhā sā siddhā siddhasaṃmatā śaśaṃsa śabarī vṛddhā rāmāya pratyupasthitā
english: Thus questioned by Rāma, that ascetic, accomplished and honored by the accomplished, the aged Śabarī, presented herself before Rāma and spoke.

sanskrit: citrakūṭaṃ tvayi prāpte vimānair atulaprabhaiḥ itas te divam ārūḍhā yān ahaṃ paryacāriṣam
english: "When you reached Citrakūṭa, those whom I used to serve ascended from here to heaven in celestial chariots of incomparable splendor.

sanskrit: taiś cāham uktā dharmajñair mahābhāgair maharṣibhiḥ āgamiṣyati te rāmaḥ supuṇyam imam āśramam
english: And those great seers, knowers of dharma and of great fortune, told me: 'Rāma will come to this most holy hermitage of yours.

sanskrit: sa te pratigrahītavyaḥ saumitrisahito 'tithiḥ taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā varāṃl lokān akṣayāṃs tvaṃ gamiṣyasi
english: He, together with the son of Sumitrā, is to be received by you as a guest, and upon seeing him you will depart to the highest and imperishable worlds.'

sanskrit: mayā tu vividhaṃ vanyaṃ saṃcitaṃ puruṣarṣabha tavārthe puruṣavyāghra pampāyās tīrasaṃbhavam
english: By me, O bull among men, O tiger among men, various forest fruits growing on the banks of Pampā have been gathered for your sake."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa dharmātmā śabaryā śabarīm idam rāghavaḥ prāha vijñāne tāṃ nityam abahiṣkṛtām
english: Thus addressed by Śabarī, the righteous Rāghava spoke these words to Śabarī, who was ever excluded from no understanding:

sanskrit: danoḥ sakāśāt tattvena prabhāvaṃ te mahātmanaḥ śrutaṃ pratyakṣam icchāmi saṃdraṣṭuṃ yadi manyase
english: "The power of your great-souled teacher, truly as heard from Danu's source — I wish to witness it directly, if you think fit."

sanskrit: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā rāmavaktrād viniḥsṛtam śabarī darśayām āsa tāv ubhau tad vanaṃ mahat
english: Hearing these words issued from Rāma's mouth, Śabarī showed those two that great forest.

sanskrit: paśya meghaghanaprakhyaṃ mṛgapakṣisamākulam mataṅgavanam ity eva viśrutaṃ raghunandana
english: "Behold, O joy of the Raghus, this forest renowned as the Mataṅga grove, dense as a mass of clouds and teeming with deer and birds.

sanskrit: iha te bhāvitātmāno guravo me mahādyute juhavāṃś cakrire tīrthaṃ mantravan mantrapūjitam
english: Here, O greatly resplendent one, my teachers, whose souls were purified, performing fire-offerings, created a sacred ford, sanctified with sacred hymns just as the sacred hymns sanctify.

sanskrit: iyaṃ pratyak sthalī vedī yatra te me susatkṛtāḥ puṣpopahāraṃ kurvanti śramād udvepibhiḥ karaiḥ
english: This is the western altar where those well-honored teachers of mine offered flowers with hands trembling from the effort of austerity.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tapaḥ prabhāvena paśyādyāpi raghūttama dyotayanti diśaḥ sarvāḥ śriyā vedyo 'tulaprabhāḥ
english: By the power of their austerities, behold even now, O best of the Raghus, that the altars illumine all directions with radiance of incomparable splendor.

sanskrit: aśaknuvadbhis tair gantum upavāsaśramālasaiḥ cintite 'bhyāgatān paśya sametān sapta sāgarān
english: When they, wearied by fasting and austerity and unable to travel, merely thought of them, behold — the seven oceans came together and arrived here.

sanskrit: kṛtābhiṣekais tair nyastā valkalāḥ pādapeṣv iha adyāpi na viśuṣyanti pradeśe raghunandana
english: The bark-garments shed by them after they had bathed — even to this day they do not dry out in this spot, O joy of the Raghus.

sanskrit: kṛtsnaṃ vanam idaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śrotavyaṃ ca śrutaṃ tvayā tad icchāmy abhyanujñātā tyaktum etat kalevaram
english: This entire forest has been seen by you, and what was to be heard has been heard. I therefore wish, with your permission, to abandon this body.

sanskrit: teṣām icchāmy ahaṃ gantuṃ samīpaṃ bhāvitātmanām munīnām āśraṃmo yeṣām ahaṃ ca paricāriṇī
english: I wish to go to the presence of those sages of purified souls, whose hermitage I served as an attendant."

sanskrit: dharmiṣṭhaṃ tu vacaḥ śrutvā rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ anujānāmi gaccheti prahṛṣṭavadano 'bravīt
english: Hearing these most righteous words, Rāghava, together with Lakṣmaṇa, said with a joyful countenance: "I give you leave; go."

sanskrit: anujñātā tu rāmeṇa hutvātmānaṃ hutāśane jvalatpāvakasaṃkāśā svargam eva jagāma sā
english: Given leave by Rāma, she offered herself into the sacrificial fire and, brilliant as blazing flame, departed to heaven itself.

sanskrit: yatra te sukṛtātmāno viharanti maharṣayaḥ tat puṇyaṃ śabarīsthānaṃ jagāmātmasamādhinā
english: To that holy abode where those great seers of virtuous souls roam in delight, Śabarī departed in the absorption of her own self.

sanskrit: divaṃ tu tasyāṃ yātāyāṃ śabaryāṃ svena karmaṇā lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā cintayām āsa rāghavaḥ
english: When Śabarī had gone to heaven through her own deeds, Rāghava reflected with his brother Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: cintayitvā tu dharmātmā prabhāvaṃ taṃ mahātmanām hitakāriṇam ekāgraṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ rāghavo 'bravīt
english: Having reflected upon that power of the great-souled ones, the righteous Rāghava spoke to Lakṣmaṇa, who was single-minded and ever devoted to his welfare:

sanskrit: dṛṣṭo 'yam āśramaḥ saumya bahvāścaryaḥ kṛtātmanām viśvastamṛgaśārdūlo nānāvihagasevitaḥ
english: "This hermitage of those who have perfected their souls has been seen, O gentle one — full of great wonders, where deer and tigers live in trust, frequented by birds of many kinds.

sanskrit: saptānāṃ ca samudrāṇām eṣu tīrtheṣu lakṣmaṇa upaspṛṣṭaṃ ca vidhivat pitaraś cāpi tarpitāḥ
english: And at these sacred fords of the seven oceans, O Lakṣmaṇa, the ritual bath has been taken and the ancestors have been duly propitiated.

sanskrit: pranaṣṭam aśubhaṃ yat tat kalyāṇaṃ samupasthitam tena tv etat prahṛṣṭaṃ me mano lakṣmaṇa saṃprati
english: Whatever inauspiciousness there was has vanished, and good fortune is now at hand. Because of that, O Lakṣmaṇa, my mind is now greatly gladdened.

sanskrit: hṛdaye hi naravyāghra śubham āvirbhaviṣyati tad āgaccha gamiṣyāvaḥ pampāṃ tāṃ priyadarśanām
english: For auspiciousness will manifest itself in my heart, O tiger among men. Come then — let us go to that Pampā, lovely to behold.

sanskrit: ṛśyamūko girir yatra nātidūre prakāśate yasmin vasati dharmātmā sugrīvo 'ṃśumataḥ sutaḥ nityaṃ vālibhayāt trastaś caturbhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ
english: Near there, not too far away, the mountain Ṛśyamūka gleams, on which the righteous-souled Sugrīva, son of Aṃśumat, dwells — ever terrified by fear of Vālin, together with four monkeys.

sanskrit: abhitvare ca taṃ draṣṭuṃ sugrīvaṃ vānararṣabham tadadhīnaṃ hi me saumya sītāyāḥ parimārgaṇam
english: Hasten to meet that bull among monkeys, Sugrīva; for the search for Sītā, O gentle one, depends upon him.

sanskrit: iti bruvāṇaṃ taṃ rāmaṃ saumitrir idam abravīt gacchāvas tvaritaṃ tatra mamāpi tvarate manaḥ
english: To Rāma speaking thus, the son of Sumitrā replied: "Let us go there quickly — my mind too hastens."

sanskrit: āśramāt tu tatas tasmān niṣkramya sa viśāṃ patiḥ ājagāma tataḥ pampāṃ lakṣmaṇena sahābhibhūḥ
english: That lord of men then departed from the hermitage and came to Pampā, accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, the subduer of foes.

sanskrit: samīkṣamāṇaḥ puṣpāḍhyaṃ sarvato vipuladrumam koyaṣṭibhiś cārjunakaiḥ śatapatraiś ca kīcakaiḥ etaiś cānyaiś ca vividhair nāditaṃ tad vanaṃ mahat
english: Gazing upon it, rich with blossoms, filled everywhere with great trees, that vast forest resonant with herons, arjuna birds, śatapatra cranes, kīcaka reeds, and many other varied creatures.

sanskrit: sa rāmo vidhivān vṛkṣān sarāṃsi vividhāni ca paśyan kāmābhisaṃtapto jagāma paramaṃ hradam
english: Rāma, duly observing the trees and the various lakes, tormented by longing, proceeded toward the supreme lake.

sanskrit: sa tām āsādya vai rāmo dūrād udakavāhinīm mataṅgasarasaṃ nāma hradaṃ samavagāhata
english: Approaching from afar the water-bearing river, Rāma plunged into the lake known as the Mataṅga pool.

sanskrit: sa tu śokasamāviṣṭo rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ viveśa nalinīṃ pampāṃ paṅkajaiś ca samāvṛtām
english: That son of Daśaratha, Rāma, overcome with grief, entered the lotus-filled Pampā, covered with water-lilies.

sanskrit: tilakāśokapuṃnāgabakuloddāla kāśinīm ramyopavanasaṃbādhāṃ padmasaṃpīḍitodakām
english: — adorned with tilaka, aśoka, puṃnāga, bakula, and uddāla trees, gleaming with kāśī blossoms, crowded with beautiful groves, its waters pressed thick with lotuses —

sanskrit: sphaṭikopamatoyāḍhyāṃ ślakṣṇavālukasaṃtatām matsyakacchapasaṃbādhāṃ tīrasthadrumaśobhitām
english: — filled with water resembling crystal, spread with fine sand, teeming with fish and tortoises, adorned by trees standing on its banks —

sanskrit: sakhībhir iva yuktābhir latābhir anuveṣṭitām kiṃnaroragagandharvayakṣarākṣasasevitām nānādrumalatākīrṇāṃ śītavārinidhiṃ śubhām
english: — entwined by creepers as if by dear companions, frequented by kiṃnaras, serpents, gandharvas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas, strewn with trees and creepers of every kind, that auspicious repository of cool waters —

sanskrit: padmaiḥ saugandhikais tāmrāṃ śuklāṃ kumudamaṇḍalaiḥ nīlāṃ kuvalayoddhātair bahuvarṇāṃ kuthām iva
english: — copper-red with fragrant lotuses, white with clusters of kumuda lilies, blue with the mass of kuvalaya flowers — many-hued like a decorated carpet —

sanskrit: aravindotpalavatīṃ padmasaugandhikāyutām puṣpitāmravaṇopetāṃ barhiṇodghuṣṭanāditām
english: — abounding in aravinda and utpala lotuses, rich with fragrant padma blossoms, flanked by forests of flowering mango trees, resounding with the cries of peacocks —

sanskrit: sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvā tataḥ pampāṃ rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha vilalāpa ca tejasvī kāmād daśarathātmajaḥ
english: Beholding that Pampā, Rāma — that splendid son of Daśaratha — together with the son of Sumitrā, broke into lamentation out of longing.

sanskrit: tilakair bījapūraiś ca vaṭaiḥ śukladrumais tathā puṣpitaiḥ karavīraiś ca puṃnāgaiś ca supuṣpitaiḥ
english: — with tilaka trees, citron trees, vaṭa figs, śukladruma trees, blossoming karavīra shrubs, and abundantly flowering puṃnāga trees —

sanskrit: mālatīkundagulmaiś ca bhaṇḍīrair niculais tathā aśokaiś ca saptaparṇaiś ca ketakair atimuktakaiḥ anyaiś ca vividhair vṛkṣaiḥ pramadevopaśobhitām
english: — with clusters of mālatī and kunda blossoms, bhaṇḍīra figs, niculas, aśokas, saptaparṇas, ketaka reeds, atimukta vines, and many other varied trees — embellished like a woman in her prime —

sanskrit: asyās tīre tu pūrvoktaḥ parvato dhātumaṇḍitaḥ ṛśyamūka iti khyātaś citrapuṣpitakānanaḥ
english: On the bank of this lake stands the mountain spoken of before, adorned with mineral ores, known as Ṛśyamūka, with its grove of varied blossoms.

sanskrit: harir ṛkṣarajo nāmnaḥ putras tasya mahātmanaḥ adhyāste taṃ mahāvīryaḥ sugrīva iti viśrutaḥ
english: The son of that great-souled Ṛkṣarajas, mighty in valor, known as Sugrīva, dwells upon that mountain.

sanskrit: sugrīvam abhigaccha tvaṃ vānarendraṃ nararṣabha ity uvāca punar vākyaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ satyavikramam
english: "Go to Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, O bull among men" — so Rāma again spoke these words to Lakṣmaṇa, whose valor was true.

sanskrit: tato mahad vartma ca dūrasaṃkramaṃ krameṇa gatvā pravilokayan vanam dadarśa pampāṃ śubhadarśa kānanām anekanānāvidhapakṣisaṃkulām
english: Then, proceeding gradually along the great road and the distant crossing, and gazing out over the forest, he beheld Pampā — beautiful to behold, its groves crowded with many birds of diverse and varied kinds.
